title: SequenceBuilder
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchCard steps, each with MonarchDurationInput for the wait, MonarchTextField for the subject, a vertical TextField in MonarchFormField for the message, a Menu of variables, a DisclosureGroup with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch) for the preview, and a reorder Menu with accessibilityActions
summary: A recipe, not a component: a multi-step outreach sequence where each step waits a duration then sends a message on a channel, with variables inserted as {{token}} and a preview with sample data.
whenToUse: In a CRM or marketing app where people define follow-up emails and messages that are sent after set delays.
whenNotToUse: For the actions of a rule use MonarchActionEditor; for a single scheduled message use a DatePicker with a message field; for a fixed onboarding list use MonarchOnboardingChecklist.
api: MonarchDurationInput.init(_ label: String, minutes: Binding<Int?>, …, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, …)
MonarchTextField.init(_ label: String, text: Binding<String>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, isSecure: Bool = false)
MonarchFormField.init(_ label: String, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, …, @ViewBuilder control: () -> Control)
TextField(_ title: String, text: Binding<String>, axis: Axis).lineLimit(_ limit: ClosedRange<Int>)
Menu(_ title: String, systemImage: String, content: () -> Content)

states.name: steps
states.description: Each step is a card titled "Step 1, Email" with the wait, the subject (email only), the message, Insert a variable and a folded preview.

states.name: straight away
states.description: A wait of 0 reads "Sent straight away" under the duration.

states.name: incomplete
states.description: An empty subject or message shows "Write a subject line." or "Write the message." with an icon.

states.name: preview
states.description: Opening the preview shows the subject and message with sample values in place of {{firstName}} and {{product}}.

states.name: full
states.description: The add buttons are disabled at the app's step limit (20 in the example).

appearance: Steps are MonarchCards on the surface role; fields, errors and the preview use their Monarch components and roles, and adapt to the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web SequenceBuilder is a component with channels and variables as data, validateSequence, findTemplateVariables and renderSequenceTemplate helpers, inserts variables at the cursor and checks message length per channel. On iOS it is a recipe of existing components that the app owns: variables are appended to the message (SwiftUI's TextField does not expose the cursor before iOS 18), the app validates and renders templates itself as in the example, and reordering is a Menu plus accessibility actions instead of drag. It is marked experimental until a Rook app adopts it. Android plans the same recipe.
accessibility: Each step card is a container named "Step 1, Email" whose title has the header trait.
Move up and Move down are accessibility actions on each card, and "Moved to position 2." is announced.
The reorder menu and remove button are icon-only with spoken names ("Reorder step 1", "Remove step 1").
MonarchDurationInput, MonarchTextField and MonarchFormField label every field and read their errors as hints.
The preview is a Monarch disclosure group that reads Expanded or Collapsed.
edgeCases: Unknown variables stay as written in the preview; validate them before saving.
A wait of 0 on the first step sends at the start of the sequence.
Long messages grow the field up to eight lines, then scroll.
